ITQAN:v1p53/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p53/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p53/r5.claim: Another view excepts the nine verses beginning “Have you seen the one who turned away?” from al-Najm's Meccan classification.
ITQAN:v1p53/r5.anchor: وقيل ﴿ أفرأيت الذي تولى ﴾ الآيات التسع

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.claim: Islahi wonders at people who boast of Abrahamic or Mosaic association and expect high rank while withholding charity, since those scriptures teach that no one bears another's burden and each faces the fruit of his own deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.anchor: the most prominent teaching of Abraham (sws) and Moses (sws) was that in the Hereafter no one will bear the burden of another person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.speaker: our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.claim: Exegetes generally identify the person in the passage as Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, a Quraysh chief, and recount his abandoned plan to embrace Islam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.anchor: Our exegetes generally regard ﻟﺬيۡ to be a reference to Wal īd ibn al-Mughīrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.speaker: our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.claim: Exegetes report that a companion promised to shield Walīd from the Hereafter if he paid money; Walīd abandoned conversion, promised payment, then paid only part.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.anchor: Though this incident has been cited by all our exegetes,

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.claim: Islahi says the report has no sound chain and, even if true, its connection to these verses is unclear; the Qur’an is not rebuking Walīd for breaking a promise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.anchor: in the first place it does not have a sound chain of narration, and if it is supposed that this incident is true

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.claim: He criticizes exegetes for treating the generic relative al-ladhī or al as a proper noun, then inventing a person and an ill-fitting incident to explain it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.anchor: they start looking for a person whom these words qualify.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.claim: The relative forms al-ladhī and al can also introduce a parable that portrays a group’s collective character through a specific figure.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.anchor: at certain instances, they are used to portray a parable too. At such instances, the purpose is to present the collective character of a group

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.claim: The woman in 16:92 who unravels her spun thread is a symbolic example, not a particular old woman whose identity and biography need investigation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.anchor: it does not refer to a specific old lady so that one may start investigating her name, family and whereabouts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.claim: A hypothetical miserly idolater represents Arabs who refuse to spend yet expect Paradise through alleged deities and racial superiority; Walīd, Abū Jahl, and other wealthy Quraysh see themselves in it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.anchor: a hypothetical character is portrayed to the Idolaters of Arabia.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.claim: The discourse uses disparaging, sarcastic irony toward people who give grudgingly yet act as if they can already see Paradise’s luxuries.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.anchor: The style of the discourse in these verses is disparaging and sarcastic:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r1.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r1.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and Muqatil say the passage concerned al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who approached Islam then turned back after a polytheist promised to bear his afterlife burden for payment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد ومقاتل: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة، كان قد سمع قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who paid five falāʾis to a poor emigrant to induce apostasy and promised to carry his sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو النضر بن الحارث، أعطى خمس فلايس لفقير من المهاجرين حتى ارتد عن دينه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r3.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the passage was revealed about al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil al-Sahmi, who sometimes agreed with the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في العاصي بن وائل السهمي، كان ربما يوافق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb identifies Abu Jahl, who acknowledged that Muhammad commanded noble morals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r4.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: في أبي جهل بن هشام، قال: والله ما يأمر محمد إلا بمكارم الأخلاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi also report that it concerned ʿUthman, who gave charity before his foster brother ʿAbd Allah ibn Saʿd ibn Abi Sarh urged him to turn back in a similar story.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس والسدي أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان، رضي الله تعالى عنه كان يتصدق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya rejects all these accounts as false and declares ʿUthman innocent of such conduct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وذلك كله عندي باطل، وعثمان رضي الله عنه منزه عن مثله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r7.claim: Here afaraʾaytum means “tell me”; its first object is the relative clause and its second is the interrogative sentence that follows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r7.anchor: فرأيت هنا بمعنى: أخبرني، ومفعولها الأول الموصول، والثاني الجملة الاستفهامية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r8.claim: Tawalla means that he turned away from Islam.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead interprets tawalla as leaving one's post at Uhud, because he takes the verse to concern ʿUthman.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: تولى: ترك المركز يوم أحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r10.claim: When the Qurʾan uses tawalla without qualification, it most often metaphorically means not entering faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r10.anchor: وإذا ذكر التولي غير مقيد في القرآن، فأكثر استعماله أنه استعارة عن عدم الدخول في الإيمان

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r6.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r6.claim: Some extend the proposed Madinan dating to verse 33.

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r1.claim: Some exegetes say the verse concerns al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra: after the Prophet's admonition moved him, a man dissuaded him, promised to bear his sins for payment, and he gave part before turning away.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r1.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين : نزلت الآية في الوليد

RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r2.claim: Some say it concerned ʿUthmān, who stopped almsgiving after his maternal half-brother ʿAbd Allāh b. Saʿd offered to bear his sins; Rāzī rejects this as unestablished and contrary to ʿUthmān's character.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : نزلت في عثمان رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r3.claim: Rāzī treats the referent broadly as anyone turning away from the reminder out of self-sufficiency, a type already mentioned in 53:29; such a person seeks other pursuits instead of attending its reminder.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r3.anchor: وكان التولي من جملة أنواعه تولى المستغني

RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r4.claim: The prefixed فاء follows the prior account of God's knowledge, power, and recompense: since people need the Prophet's teaching and following to avoid major sins, turning away follows a state of extreme need.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r4.anchor: هو ما تقدم من بيان علم الله وقدرته

RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r5.claim: Some exegetes take الذي as a particular known man, namely al-Walīd; Rāzī instead reads it as the previously mentioned general class of those who turned away.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r5.anchor: على ما قال بعض المفسرين عائد إلى معلوم

RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r6.claim: Although من is general, Arabic commonly resumes it according to its singular wording, as in 28:84, من جاء بالحسنة فله, rather than according to its plural sense.

RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r3.claim: Rāzī's broader reading is that the man turned from revelation while seeking only worldly life, giving little toward what was due to secure the affairs of the afterlife and then stopping.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r3.anchor: تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r1.claim: Akdā derives from al-kudyah, hard rock encountered while digging; the verb can mean that a well digger hit rock.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r1.anchor: Withheld translates akdā, which derives from

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r4.claim: Those who think past deeds suffice or consider themselves pure and stop doing good may find even earlier deeds come to nothing.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r4.anchor: when people are satisfied that past deeds will suffice or consider themselves pure and consequently cease to perform good deeds, even past deeds may come to naught.

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r6.claim: Though applicable to anyone ignoring others’ needs, the verses were reportedly revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, who conditionally offered a Prophet follower money to return to Quraysh religion, then paid only part.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r6.anchor: these verses were reportedly revealed in relation to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah

BURSEVI:v9p200/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r3.claim: The person turned away from following the truth and remaining steadfast in it.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r3.anchor: أي أعرض عن اتباع الحق والثبات عليه

BURSEVI:v9p200/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r6.speaker: قالوا
BURSEVI:v9p200/r6.claim: They report that the verses came down about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who listened to the Prophet and considered accepting Islam; an idolater reproached him for leaving ancestral religion.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r6.anchor: قالوا : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة كان يتبع رسول الله عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v9p200/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r7.claim: Fearing punishment, al-Walīd accepted a promise that another would bear it, paid part of the promised money, then turned away from preaching and withheld the rest.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r7.anchor: فضمن أن يتحمل عنه العذاب وكل شيء يخافه في الآخرة إن أعطاه بعض ماله

BURSEVI:v9p200/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r10.claim: Bursevī says the main censure concerns turning away and the false belief that another can bear one's punishment; the gift's cessation merely narrates the episode, with irony.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r10.anchor: الظاهر أن الآية مسوقة لذم التولي وسوء الاعتقاد في نفع التحمل يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v9p200/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r12.claim: The seeker spends a small part of life's capital on the spiritual path, then tires, returns to sensual ego, and spends the rest on worldly pleasure; this relapse reflects lack of readiness for union.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r12.anchor: إشارة إلى السالك المنقطع في أثناء السلوك الراجع من السير إلى الله إلى نفسه البشرية

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r1.speaker: أسباب النزول
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r1.claim: Reported occasions of revelation describe a Muslim who spent generously in God’s cause, was warned by others that he would become poor and promised they would bear his sins, then stopped spending; these verses were revealed about the incident.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r1.anchor: أن رجلا من المسلمين كان ينفق من ماله في سبيل الله فلامه بعض الناس على كثرة الإنفاق

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r2.claim: The story and citations from Moses’ and Abraham’s scriptures clarify the truth against the polytheists’ claim that idols represented God’s daughters, the angels, whom they worshiped for intercession; earlier verses refuted that claim.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r2.anchor: أشار سبحانه بالتعرض لهذه القصة ونقل ما من صحف إبراهيم وموسى عليهما السلام إلى بيان وجه الحق فيها

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r3.claim: The passage establishes that creation and governance belong to God and lead to a second life of recompense, which entails revealed religion and duties; the destruction of Noah’s, ‘Ad’s, Thamud’s, and the overturned cities’ peoples is evidence.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r3.anchor: وهو أن الخلق والتدبير لله سبحانه، إليه ينتهي كل ذلك

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r4.claim: After these scriptural teachings, the surah warns that this warner belongs to the earlier warners, says the Hour is near, and ends by commanding prostration and worship.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r4.anchor: ثم عقب سبحانه هذا الذي نقله عن صحف النبيين الكريمين بالتنبيه على أن هذا النذير من النذر الأولى الخالية

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r5.claim: Here turning away means turning away from spending in God’s cause, as the next verse clarifies.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r5.anchor: التولي هو الإعراض والمراد به بقرينة الآية التالية الإعراض عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r7.claim: The prefixed fa in ‘Have you seen?’ branches the question from the preceding discussion.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r7.anchor: والتفريع الذي في قوله { أفرأيت } مبني على ما قدمنا

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r8.claim: The question asks the listener to consider someone who abandoned spending, gave a small amount, then stopped giving altogether.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r8.anchor: والمعنى فأخبرني عمن أعرض عن الإنفاق وأعطى قليلا من المال وأمسك بعد ذلك أشد الإمساك

TABRISI:53:31-41/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي وجماعة من المفسرين
TABRISI:53:31-41/r11.claim: They report the passage about ʿUthmān: after his foster brother ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ promised to bear his sins if he stopped donating, ʿUthmān gave him a camel and ceased giving; it says he left his post at Uḥud, then resumed his former practice.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r11.anchor: فعاد عثمان إلى ما كان عليه عن ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي وجماعة من المفسرين

TABRISI:53:31-41/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r12.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
TABRISI:53:31-41/r12.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd say the verses concern al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who returned to shirk after a critic pledged to carry his punishment, paid the man only part of the promised amount, then withheld the rest.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r12.anchor: فنزلت أفرأيت الذي تولى عن الإيمان وأعطى صاحبه الضامن قليلا وأكدى

TABRISI:53:32-39/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r9.claim: The person turned away from the truth.

THALABI:v9p150#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك
THALABI:v9p150#2/r1.claim: These authorities say the passage concerns Uthman: his foster-brother Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh warned that charity would leave him penniless and offered to bear his sins for his camel and gear; Uthman gave it, stopped some charity, then resumed it. The turning away is linked to leaving his position at Uhud.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك

THALABI:v9p150#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
THALABI:v9p150#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd say it concerns al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who accepted Islam, was shamed for leaving his ancestors’ religion, then paid a scolder who promised to bear his punishment; al-Walid gave part of the money and withheld the rest.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن زيد: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة، وكان قد اتبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على دينه

THALABI:v9p150#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p150#2/r4.claim: In this account, the turning away means turning back from faith, the small gift goes to the guarantor, and akdā means withholding the promised remainder.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r4.anchor: فأنزل الله سبحانه أفرأيت الذي تولى أدبر عن الإيمان وأعطى يعني صاحبه الضامن قليلا وأكدى بخل بالباقي

THALABI:v9p150#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r6.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
THALABI:v9p150#2/r6.claim: Ata ibn Yasar reports that the passage concerned a man who set out to visit the Prophet seeking good, but a pagan offered to take his provisions and bear his sin; the man accepted.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r6.anchor: وروى موسى بن عبيدة الزبيدي عن عطاء بن يسار قال

THALABI:v9p151/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r1.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v9p151/r1.claim: Al-Suddi gives another occasion: it was revealed about al-As ibn Waʾil, who sometimes agreed with the Prophet on certain matters.
THALABI:v9p151/r1.anchor: وروي عن السدي أيضا قال: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي، وذلك أنه كان ربما يوافق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض الأمور

THALABI:v9p151/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
THALABI:v9p151/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says it concerned Abu Jahl, who admitted Muhammad commanded noble manners but did not believe.
THALABI:v9p151/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: نزلت في أبي جهل، وذلك أنه قال: والله ما يأمرنا محمد إلا بمكارم الأخلاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p63/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p63/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p63/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Muqatil, and Ibn Zayd say this was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who had followed Muhammad but turned back after a polytheist offered to bear his punishment in return for money; al-Walid paid some of it and reverted to shirk.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p63/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة وهو قول مجاهد، ومقاتل، وابن زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p63/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p63/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p63/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil explain تولى as turning away from truth and Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p63/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومقاتل: أدبر عن الحق والإسلام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r4.claim: The person who turned away from belief was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r4.anchor: أعرض عن الإيمان، يعني: الوليد بن المغيرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r5.claim: After al-Walid accepted the Prophet's message, a polytheist rebuked him; al-Walid feared punishment, then returned to shirk when promised that another would bear his punishment for payment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r5.anchor: وكان قد اتبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فعيره بعض المشركين على ذلك فقال: إني أخشى عذاب الله

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r1.speaker: Mücâhid ve İbn Zeyd
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r1.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd report that Walid ibn al-Mughira listened to the Prophet and neared Islam, but a polytheist promised to bear his afterlife burden for payment; Walid turned back, paid a little, then stopped.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r1.anchor: Mücâhid’den ve İbn Zeyd’den rivayet olunduğu üzere Velîd b. Muğīre Resûlullah’ın meclisine gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.claim: Tafsīr reports connect these verses with episodes showing some polytheists’ fickle conduct, but the reports are unreliable and their narrative details sit uneasily with Qur’anic principles.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.anchor: bunların sağlam haberler olmadığı anlaşılmaktadır; ayrıca olayların kurgusunda Kur’an’ın ilkelerine göre izahı kolay olmayan unsurlar bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r3.claim: The target is someone who may briefly feel compassion but remains attached to worldly wealth and persists in stinginess through a rigid, imposing attitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r3.anchor: –bazan merhamete gelse de– dünya ve mal tutkusundan kurtulamayan, katı ve dayatmacı bir tavırla hasisliğini sürdürenler eleştirilmektedir

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r2.claim: Ikrima reports that during an expedition a man unable to find a mount asked a friend for help; the friend offered a ride in exchange for taking on his sins, and these verses were revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج في غزوة فجاء رجل يريد أن يحمل فلم يجد ما يخرج عليه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r3.speaker: دراج أبو السميع
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r3.claim: Darraj Abu al-Samih gives another expedition account: after the Prophet could not carry a man, another person offered a mount so he could catch the army with his good deeds; the passage through 53:41 was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r3.anchor: عن دراج أبي السميع قال خرجت سرية غازية فسأل رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يحمله

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says a convert’s former co-religionist offered to assume his sins if he paid; the convert gave money, was pressed for more, and signed a witnessed agreement, prompting the verses.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال ان رجلا أسلم فلقيه بعض من يعيره فقال أتركت دين الأشياخ

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, and al-Musayyib ibn Sharik say these verses concern Uthman, who paused his charity after his foster brother promised to bear his sins, then resumed his generous giving.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك: نزلت في عثمان بن عفان

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r3.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd instead identify al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: after accepting Islam, he gave a man some promised wealth to shoulder his punishment, then withheld the rest and returned to polytheism.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن زيد: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

NAHHAS:v4p274/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v4p274/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says the passage concerns a man who accepted Islam, then turned away after a friend shamed him and offered to bear his punishment in exchange for a little money.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r12.anchor: قال ابن زيد نزلت في رجل أسلم فلقيه صاحبه فغيره وقال له أضللت أباك

SAMIN-DURR:53:34/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:34/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:34/r2.claim: The neighboring expression أرأيت means tell me.
SAMIN-DURR:53:34/r2.anchor: أو لم يتممه. وأرأيت بمعنى أخبرني.

ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n28/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n28/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n28/r1.claim: Asad bases his rendering of 53:33–34, including its bracketed interpretive insertions, on Razi's reading that the passage returns to an earlier theme; the excerpt cuts off before identifying the verses.
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n28/r1.anchor: Razi's convincing interpretation of this passage as a return to the theme touched upon in verses

QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#1/r1.claim: Dropping the hamza of raʾā facilitates pronunciation while leaving the grammar unchanged.
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#1/r1.anchor: Hamza of raʾā dropped entirely (tashīl) — phonological facilitation; grammatically identical to standard

QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#2/r1.claim: The hamza is lengthened into ā by madd badal, adding emphatic stretch and rhetorical weight to the question.
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#2/r1.anchor: Hamza prolonged into long ā vowel (madd badal) — emphatic stretching of the interrogative

QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#3/r1.claim: This dialectal variant realizes the hamza as a transitional glottal stop between full hamza and elision.
QIRAAT-ER:53:33:2#3/r1.anchor: Hamza realized as transitional glottal stop — intermediate between full hamza and complete elision

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65/r1.claim: The person turned away from following truth and remaining steadfast in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65/r1.anchor: أي عن اتباع الحق والثبات عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r9.claim: Here afara'ayta means tell me; its first object is the relative pronoun and its second is the following interrogative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r9.anchor: و ( أفرأيت ) هنا على ما في البحر بمعنى أخبرني ومفعولها الأول الموصول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: after following Muhammad, he was shamed by a polytheist who promised to bear his punishment if he returned to shirk; al-Walid returned, paid part of the promised money, and withheld the rest.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة، كان قد اتبع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على دينه فعيره بعض المشركين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413#2/r2.claim: The one who turned away is the person who turned away from faith.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r1.claim: The person turned away from following the truth and remaining steadfast in it.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r1.claim: The passage is framed by early apostasy after the Prophet recited the great signs of the Night Journey; when he prostrated at the end of this surah, Muslims, polytheists, jinn, and humans prostrated too, unexpectedly even to later apostates; the source cites Bukhari.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r1.anchor: وكان لما نزلت عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم سجدة النجم وسجد فيها صلى الله عليه وسلم سجد معه - كما في البخاري - المسلمون والمشركون والجن والإنس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r2.claim: The person turned away from remembrance after having been devoted to it and thinking himself and his family firmly rooted in faith; the wording also applies to apostates, hypocrites, and those who abandon good works after belief.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r2.anchor: { الذي تلى * } أي عن ذكرنا عبد أن كان حريصا عليه , يظن هو وأهله أنه عريق في أهله بإيمانه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r5.claim: A reported occasion identifies the man as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: he accepted Islam, then apostatized after a polytheist taunted him and promised to bear his punishment if he returned.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r5.anchor: قيل : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة أسلم ثم ارتد لتعيير بعض المشركين له , وقوله له ( ارجع وأنا أتحمل عنك العذاب )

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r3.claim: Ikrima says the verses were revealed about a man on an expedition who lacked a mount and accepted a friend's camel in exchange for taking on the friend's sins.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج في مغزاة فجاء رجل فلم يجد ما يخرج عليه فلقي صديقا له فقال: أعطني شيئا

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.speaker: دراج أبو السمح
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.claim: Darraj says the passage was revealed after a man who could not get a mount from the Prophet was offered transport by another man so he could catch the army.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.anchor: عن دراج أبي السمح قال: خرجت سرية غازية فسأل رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يحمله فقال: لا أجد ما أحملك عليه

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verses concern a new Muslim who feared God but was offered relief from all punishment by an opponent if he paid; he paid a little, then bargained, and documented the deal.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: إن رجلا أسلم فلقيه بعض من يعيره فقال: أتركت دين الأشياخ وضللتهم وزعمت أنهم في النار

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies the person who turned away as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who used to visit the Prophet and Abu Bakr and listen.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أفرأيت الذي تولى} قال: الوليد بن المغيرة كان يأتي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبا بكر فيسمع ما يقولان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r4.claim: This parenthetical warning falls between God's knowledge and the account in 53:33; its fāʾ warns believers against pride in good deeds or others' praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r4.anchor: وجملة { فلا تزكوا أنفسكم } اعتراض بين جملة { هو أعلم بكم } وجملة { أفرأيت الذي تولى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r1.claim: The fāʾ introduces astonishment after 53:31's promise of recompense: this person's actions misunderstand God's purpose and the fact that each has only what they strive for.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r1.anchor: الفاء لتفريع الاستفهام التعجيبي على قوله : { ليجزي الذين أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزي الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r2.claim: Unlike the group in 53:29, this is a particular person; commentators agree, and al-ladhī points more clearly to one individual than man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r2.anchor: فالذي تولى وأعطى قليلا هو هنا ليس فريقا مثل الذي عناه قوله : { فأعرض عن من تولى عن ذكرنا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and al-Qurṭubī report Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd's identification as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra: after nearing Islam, he was rebuked by a polytheist, paid him to bear his punishment, then stopped paying and returned to shirk.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد وابنن زيد أن المراد به الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī transmits al-Suddī's identification as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r4.anchor: وروى القرطبي عن السدي : أنها نزلت في العاصي بن وائل السهمي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r5.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said the verse was revealed about Abū Jahl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r5.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب : نزلت في أبي جهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said it was revealed about al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r6.anchor: وعن الضحاك : نزلت في النضر بن الحارث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r7.speaker: الواحدي والثعلبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r7.claim: Al-Wāḥidī's Asbāb al-Nuzūl and al-Kashshāf report that it was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ, who dissuaded ʿUthmān from charity before his conversion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r7.anchor: ووقع في ( أسباب النزول ) للواحدي و ( الكشاف ) أنها نزلت في عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the Ibn Abī Sarḥ report as false because ʿUthmān would not have listened to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وذلك باطل وعثمان منزه عن مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r1.claim: The phrase indicates he turned from considering Islam after nearly embracing it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r1.anchor: فأشار قوله تعالى : { الذي تولى } إلى أنه تولى عن النظر في الإسلام بعد أن قاربه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r3.claim: Turning away is blame, not part of the astonishment; ‘gave little’ prepares blame for stinginess even with a little, then cutting the gift off, beyond remaining in disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r3.anchor: وليس وصفه ب { تولى } داخلا في التعجيب ولكنه سيق مساق الذم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.claim: He acted as though paying someone to carry the consequences of abandoning Islam would avert punishment, assuming both that turning away was a crime and that afterlife sins could be transferred.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.anchor: والمعنى : أنه آمن نفسه من تبعة التولي عن الإسلام ببذل شيء لمن تحمل عنه تبعة توليه كأنه يعلم الغيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r11.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r11.claim: They identify the person as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who heard the Prophet, sat with him, and came near Islam before being pressured to return to his fathers’ religion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد وغيرهما نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي وذلك أنه سمع قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجلس إليه ووعظه رسول الله، فقرب من الإسلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r12.claim: A polytheist promised to bear al-Walīd’s afterlife liability for money; al-Walīd agreed, turned back from Islam, paid part, then withheld the rest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r12.anchor: وأنا أتحمل لك بكل شيء تخافه في الآخرة، لكن على أن تعطيني كذا وكذا من المال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r13.speaker: الثعلبي عن قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r13.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī reports that it concerned ʿUthmān and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as false and says ʿUthmān is innocent of it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r13.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي عن قوم أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان في قصة جرت له مع عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح وذلك كله عندي باطل، وعثمان رضي الله عنه منزه عن مثله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r16.claim: Tawallā means turning back or away from God’s command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r16.anchor: و: تولى معناه: أدبر وأعرض ومعناه عن أمر الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r1.claim: They identify the man as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra: after turning to the Prophet’s religion, he was shamed by a pagan for abandoning ancestral faith, promised wealth to return to shirk, gave some, then withheld the rest.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r1.anchor: أنه الوليد بن المغيرة وكان قد تبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على دينه فعيره بعض المشركين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the man as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who gave some poor Muslims five she-camels to apostatize and promised to bear their sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r2.anchor: أنه النضر بن الحارث أعطى بعض الفقراء المسلمين خمس قلائص حتى ارتد عن إسلامه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r3.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī identifies the man as Abū Jahl, who said Muhammad only commanded noble character.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r3.anchor: أنه أبو جهل وذلك أنه قال والله ما يأمرنا محمد إلا بمكارم الأخلاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the man as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī, who sometimes agreed with the Prophet on certain matters.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r4.anchor: أنه العاص بن وائل السهمي وكان ربما وافق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض الأمور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p77#2/r5.claim: Tawallā here means that the man turned away from faith.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir condemns turning away from obedience, connecting it to the description in 75:31–32: neither believing nor praying, but denying and turning away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذاما لمن تولى عن طاعة الله: {فلا صدق ولا صلى. ولكن كذب وتولى} [القيامة: 31، 32]

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي وجماعة من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r1.claim: One occasion account identifies ʿUthmān: his milk-brother ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ persuaded him to give money in exchange for bearing sins; he curtailed charity, then resumed his best conduct after revelation.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r1.anchor: قيل: نزل في عثمان، كان ينفق ماله في سبيل الخير، فلامه عبد الله بن سعد بن شراحه

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r2.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the verses concern al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who followed the Prophet, then gave a pagan a little to assume his sins and withheld the rest after being taunted.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r2.anchor: وقيل: بل نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r4.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār reports a man set out to meet Muhammad for good, but a disbeliever took his provisions and promised to bear his sin.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r4.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في رجل قال لأهله: جهزوني أنطلق إلى محمد أصب منه خيرا

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r5.speaker: السدي
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says the verses concern al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who sometimes agreed with the Prophet on certain matters.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r5.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي، كان ربما يوافق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r3.claim: Turning away means leaving one's position at Uhud; Uthman later returned to better conduct.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r3.anchor: ومعنى { تولى } ترك المركز يوم أحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r1.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r1.claim: The person who turned away was al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه العاص بن وائل السهمي ، قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies him as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who visited the Prophet and Abu Bakr, heard them, then turned away.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r2.anchor: أنه الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي ، قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r3.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies him as al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who gave five camels to a poor emigrant apostate and promised to bear the sin of his return.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r3.anchor: أنه النضر بن الحارث أعطى خمس قلائص لفقير من المهاجرين حين ارتد عن دينه

MUQATIL:53:33-42/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r1.claim: The one who turned away from truth is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r1.anchor: عن الحق يعني الوليد بن المغيرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#2/r1.claim: The person turned away from faith.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ أفرأيت الذي تولى ﴾ اعرض عن الايمان

QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r1.claim: After explaining the idolaters' ignorance, the passage singles out one of them for bad conduct.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r1.anchor: لما بين جهل المشركين في عبادة الأصنام ذكر واحدا منهم معينا بسوء فعله

QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r2.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r2.claim: They say it concerned al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who accepted Islam, was shamed by a polytheist, promised payment to return to shirk, paid some, then withheld the rest.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد ومقاتل: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r4.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r4.claim: Another report from Muqatil says al-Walid gave the Prophet a pledge of faith and then turned away.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r4.anchor: وعنه أنه أعطى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عقد الإيمان ثم تولى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r5.claim: They identify ʿUthman: his foster brother promised to bear his sins for a camel and gear; ʿUthman gave it, stopped some charity, then resumed good works.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك: نزلت في عثمان بن عفان

QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r6.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r6.claim: Al-Suddi also says it concerned al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, who sometimes agreed with the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r6.anchor: وقال السدي أيضا: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r5.claim: The person described as turning away has turned away from the truth.
